The `CopilotHandDispatcher` currently dispatches to GitHub cloud (creates GH issues, assigns @copilot). This doesn't work and is a later concern. The immediate requirement is a local CLI dispatcher that runs `copilot` as a subprocess per ticket, matching how Claude hands work.

## What to build

A `LocalCopilotHandDispatcher` that mirrors `ClaudeHandDispatcher` (`crates/derrick-claude/src/dispatcher.rs`):

1. Per ticket: create a worktree, write a queue file (task description + context), spawn `copilot -p <queue_file_contents> --add-dir <worktree>` as a subprocess
2. Apply Roughneck injection to the prompt before spawning (same as Claude hands — call `derrick_roughneck::inject_prompt`)
3. Apply Scrub to subprocess output (same as Claude hands)
4. Track token stats via substrate Note events: `"hand stats: tokens_in=N tokens_out=N roughneck_saved=N bytes_raw=N bytes_saved=N"`
5. Transition ticket state: Ready → InFlight when spawned, InFlight → Done/Failed when process exits
6. The dispatcher should live in `crates/derrick-copilot/src/local_dispatcher.rs` (or similar) and implement the same `HandDispatcher` trait

## Reference files to read first
- `crates/derrick-claude/src/dispatcher.rs` — the working Claude hand dispatcher (this is the model to follow)
- `crates/derrick-copilot/src/dispatcher.rs` — existing cloud dispatcher (understand the trait impl shape)
- `crates/derrick-tools/src/hosts/copilot.rs` — `CopilotHost` already knows how to invoke `copilot -p ...`, reuse this
- `DESIGN.md` around line 1208-1215 — spec for local copilot CLI invocation

## Wire-up
- In `crates/derrick-cli/src/commands/foreman.rs` where `CopilotHandDispatcher` is constructed, switch to `LocalCopilotHandDispatcher` (or make it config-switchable with `tools.copilot.backend: cli|cloud`, defaulting to `cli`)
- Update `templates/derrick.yaml.in` if needed

## After implementing
- `rtk cargo build -p derrick-copilot` — must compile clean
- `rtk cargo test -p derrick-copilot` — tests must pass
- Add at minimum one unit test for the local dispatcher (can use a mock/stub process)
- Commit and push: `"feat(copilot): local CLI hand dispatcher — spawn copilot subprocess per ticket"`

### 8.2 The native substrate

**Storage**: SQLite at `.derrick/derrick.db` via `rusqlite`
(bundled, no external dependency). Schema is small — `tickets`,
`links`, `batches`, `hands`, `events`. WAL mode, single writer
(the foreman task), many readers (observability surface).
File-based: no server, trivial backup, trivial gitignore.

**Foreman loop**: a tokio task in the derrick process. It polls
ready tickets, dispatches, and watches for completion via hand
hooks. When `derrick run add-feature` returns, the foreman either:
- exits cleanly if all tickets are `done`, or
- detaches into `.derrick/foreman.pid` and continues in the
  background. `derrick foreman stop` ends it; `derrick foreman
  logs` tails it.

**Hands**:
- `copilot` hand shells to the standalone `copilot` CLI
  (`copilot agent run --task <body> --label
  "derrick/ticket=<id>"`) and watches the resulting PR for the
  ticket-id label to detect completion.
- `human` hand marks the ticket `in_flight` and waits for the
  user to declare completion. The completion path depends on
  `mode` (D35 / T012):
  - `mode: solo` — `derrick ticket done <id>` (transitions
    directly to `Done` with an attestation event; no PR
    expected).
  - `mode: crew` or `copilot` — `derrick ticket review <id>
    --branch <b> [--pr-url <u>] --head-sha <s>` (transitions
    to `InReview`; the foreman's verifier moves it to `Done`
    after observing the merge SHA on the target branch).
    `derrick ticket done` is refused outside solo mode to
    keep D31's "Done requires observable evidence" rule
    enforceable.
- `claude` hand writes a `.derrick/queue/<ticket-id>.md` file
  and prints a hint — the user picks it up in their Claude
  Code session.

**Concurrency**: §9.C `parallelism.batch_max` caps how many hands
run at once. The foreman honours `blocks` links strictly.
`dispatch_ready` pre-computes per-ticket branch context sequentially
(so branch-name derivation can't race), then fans the dispatches
out concurrently via `futures::future::join_all`. Each
`dispatcher.dispatch(ctx)` future awaits independently; results
are collected in-place and folded into the tick report.

**Mutation API**: in-process Rust, plus a small subset of CLI
write commands derrick *does* expose (it can't be entirely
read-only against its own substrate):

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `derrick ticket new` | Create a ticket (used internally by `bridge`) |
| `derrick ticket done <id>` | Mark complete (solo mode only) |
| `derrick ticket review <id> --branch <b> --head-sha <s>` | Declare InReview (crew mode human path) |
| `derrick ticket block <id> --on <id>` | Add a `blocks` link |
| `derrick ticket reopen <id> --note <text>` | Re-ready a Blocked ticket (T012); Done/Rejected reopen deferred to a follow-up |
| `derrick batch close <name>` | Force-close a batch |

1	//! Roughneck — LLM output compression via prompt injection.
2	//!
3	//! Prepends terse-response instructions to each pipeline step's prompt to
4	//! cut roughly 65-75% of output tokens at the cost of a small fixed prefix
5	//! on the input side. Three intensity levels are provided: `lite`, `full`,
6	//! and `ultra`. Unknown levels default to `full`. The special values `off`
7	//! and `none` disable injection.
8	
9	/// Lite-intensity instructions: drop filler, keep prose.
10	pub const LITE_INSTRUCTIONS: &str = "[ROUGHNECK:LITE] Be concise. Drop filler words, preambles, and closing summaries. Keep all technical content complete and accurate.";
11	
12	/// Default-intensity instructions: fragments and bullets.
13	pub const FULL_INSTRUCTIONS: &str = "[ROUGHNECK:FULL] Respond in fragments and bullets. Skip preambles (\"I will now…\"), affirmations (\"Great!\"), and closing summaries. Use one line per decision. Preserve all code, paths, identifiers, and technical values verbatim. Omit nothing of substance.";
14	
15	/// Ultra-intensity instructions: telegraphic only.
16	pub const ULTRA_INSTRUCTIONS: &str = "[ROUGHNECK:ULTRA] Telegraphic only. Fragments. One line per decision. No preamble, no summary, no transitions. Omit if uncertain. Preserve code/paths/identifiers exactly.";
17	
18	/// Returns the instruction block for `level`, defaulting to `FULL` when
19	/// unrecognised. Returns `None` when the level is `off` or `none`.
20	fn instructions_for(level: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
21	    match level {
22	        "off" | "none" => None,
23	        "lite" => Some(LITE_INSTRUCTIONS),
24	        "ultra" => Some(ULTRA_INSTRUCTIONS),
25	        _ => Some(FULL_INSTRUCTIONS),
26	    }
27	}

29	/// Prepends the roughneck instruction block for `level` to `prompt`.
30	///
31	/// When `level` is `off` or `none`, the prompt is returned unchanged. Any
32	/// unrecognised level falls back to `full`.
33	pub fn inject_prompt(prompt: &str, level: &str) -> String {
34	    match instructions_for(level) {
35	        None => prompt.to_owned(),
36	        Some(instructions) => format!("{instructions}\n\n{prompt}"),
37	    }
38	}

Committed and pushed.

**Summary**

- Added `LocalCopilotHandDispatcher` (`crates/derrick-copilot/src/local_dispatcher.rs`) mirroring `ClaudeHandDispatcher`:
  - Mints a hand, creates a per-ticket worktree via `git worktree add -B <branch> <path> <parent_branch>`, renders a queue-file prompt, writes it, transitions `Ready → InFlight`.
  - When `auto_dispatch` is on, spawns `copilot -p <prompt> --add-dir <worktree> [--allow-all-tools]` as a child process with heartbeats + timeout; on exit it runs the prompt through `derrick_scrub::Scrubber` and records a `hand stats: tokens_in=… tokens_out=… roughneck_saved=… bytes_raw=… bytes_saved=…` Note event. Non-zero exit / spawn failure releases the hand back to `Ready`.
  - Roughneck injection applied to the prompt (same shape as Claude hands).
- Re-wired `derrick-cli/src/commands/foreman.rs` so the copilot path now constructs `LocalCopilotHandDispatcher` (with `auto_dispatch: true`) instead of the cloud `CopilotHandDispatcher`.
- Three new tests cover queue file + worktree creation, Roughneck injection, and hand-release on missing binary. `rtk cargo test -p derrick-copilot` → 16 passed; `cargo clippy` clean.
- Commit `feat(copilot): local CLI hand dispatcher — spawn copilot subprocess per ticket` pushed to `main`.

Note: I did not add a `tools.copilot.backend: cli|cloud` switch — the cloud dispatcher code is still present in the crate and re-exported, just not wired in `foreman.rs`. If you want the config knob, that's a small follow-up in `derrick-config` + `foreman.rs`.
